newsitem.title: CANADA: Bank of Canada sets specials at 3.25 percent.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Canada sets specials at 3.25 percent.

text.p: The Bank of Canada on Monday conducted a round of special purchase and resale agreements in the money market at 3.25 percent, traders said.
The central bank intervened after the call loan, or overnight lending rate, traded above the top of the bank's 2.75-3.25 percent target range, dealers said.

"Money has traded hands above the 3.25 percent level," said one Toronto-based trader. "The Bank doesn't want us to get too carried away with the backup in the United States at the moment, so he's just supplying money to offset that."
The overnight rate and Canadian T-bill yields rose this morning amid weakness in the Canadian dollar and a drop in Canadian and U.S. bond prices.
It was the fourth time in the past three sessions that the Bank of Canada intervened with specials in the money market. The bank set specials at 3.25 percent twice on Thursday and once on Friday.
The call loan rate traded at 3.25 percent following the intervention, while the three-month cash T-bill traded with a yield of 2.78 percent.
